mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ocellatin-F1 shows stronger POPC model-membrane disruption than ocellatin-LB1 and ocellatin-LB2 in calcein-loaded vesicle assays; the supported mechanism claim is model-membrane permeabilization/pore-forming capacity, not a direct pathogen-cell target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ocellatin-F1 compared with ocellatin-LB1 and ocellatin-LB2

supporting_values.value: 48% dye release at 1.57 mM; 96% at 6.28 mM

mechanism_claims.limitations: Assay uses POPC model vesicles; do not promote to a direct microbial membrane lesion without preserving the model-system boundary.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: All three peptides acquire high helical content in membrane-mimetic environments; ocellatin-F1 has stronger average helical propensity, especially in anionic POPC:POPG vesicles, consistent with stronger membrane interactions.

supporting_values.value: helicity higher than 90% at higher POPC concentrations
53.7%, 85.2%, and 60.4% for LB1, LB2, and F1 respectively

mechanism_claims.limitations: CD and vesicle assays support membrane interaction and conformational preference; exact cellular mechanism remains bounded.
